The district science project was due on the fifteenth, at the block education office in Pachora. Salma looked at the calendar hanging in her father's tailoring shop and circled the tenth instead.
Her cousin Imran, sewing buttons at the next machine, looked up. "The fifteenth is the date. Why the tenth?"
"Because the only printing shop in town shuts whenever there's a wedding season rush," Salma said. "Last year Ruksana's chart got printed on the sixteenth. And in March I had fever for four days. If that happens again, I'd have nothing."
She thought for a moment. "Five days for things I can't see coming. If nothing goes wrong, I just hand it in early."
On the eighth, the printing shop put up a sign: closed till the thirteenth. Salma had already printed her chart on the seventh.

qa.q: Until when was the printing shop closed?
qa.a: It was closed till the thirteenth.

qa.q: How might Salma have felt when she saw the printing shop's sign?
qa.a: She probably felt relieved and a bit proud, since her chart was already printed on the seventh.

qa.q: What else could Salma plan into her five spare days, and why?
qa.a: She could use one of them for a final check with her teacher, so small mistakes are fixed before the deadline.

qa.q: How might Imran see Salma's early deadline?
qa.a: Imran first wonders why she chose the tenth, but may be impressed once the printing shop closes.

grounding: It shows a student with a project due on the fifteenth aiming to finish by the tenth, knowing printing and illness often cause delays.

subtype: Approach: adds buffer days before a deadline [Thinking]
passage:
Noa's history project was due on the 15th of May, and her school in Rotterdam was strict about late work. On the 1st, she sat at the kitchen table with her planner and her brother Felix.
"I'm finishing on the 10th," she said.
"The deadline is the 15th."
"I know. But last term the school printer broke the week everything was due, and half my class handed in late. And in April I had the flu for five days." She drew a box around the 10th. "So those five days are for whatever goes wrong."
Felix shrugged. "What if nothing goes wrong?"
"Then I'm done early and I sleep."
On the 12th, the school printer broke again. Noa's project had been printed and handed in on the 10th. Felix read the class chat full of panic and looked at her. "Okay. You were right."

qa.q: On what date did the school printer break?
qa.a: On the 12th, the school printer broke again.

qa.q: How might Noa have felt when the printer broke on the 12th?
qa.a: She probably felt calm and relieved, even a little smug, since her project was already handed in.

qa.q: What else could Noa do with her spare days if nothing goes wrong?
qa.a: She could use them to start revising for other subjects, so the buffer still gives her something useful.

qa.q: How does Felix see Noa's plan in the end?
qa.a: Felix was doubtful at first, but after reading the panicked class chat he admits she was right.

grounding: It shows a student with a project due on the 15th aiming to finish by the 10th, knowing printing problems and illness often cause delays.
